result.description:
About Us
NDT TechOps Pty Ltd is an Australian engineering services company specialising in Non-Destructive Testing (NDT), inspection, asset integrity, quality assurance and technical reporting. We provide inspection and engineering support across the mining, construction, manufacturing, oil & gas and infrastructure sectors.

As our business continues to grow, we are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Contract Administrator to support the administration of engineering projects, contractual documentation and client service delivery.

About the Role
The Contract Administrator plays a key role in supporting the successful delivery of inspection and engineering projects by managing contract documentation, coordinating project administration activities and ensuring compliance with contractual obligations and company procedures.

The position works closely with project managers, engineers, NDT inspectors and clients to facilitate efficient project delivery and maintain accurate project records.

Key Responsibilities
-Administer engineering service contracts from commencement through to completion. 
-Prepare, review, and maintain contractual documentation, quotations, purchase orders, and project records. 
-Overseeing work by contractors and reporting on variations to work orders.
-Monitor contract performance against agreed terms and conditions.
-Support tender submissions and contract variations. 
-Liaise with clients, suppliers, inspectors, and project managers regarding contract administration matters. 
-Maintain confidential commercial and contractual information. 
-Manage document control processes and maintain accurate electronic records. 
-Monitor project costs and assist with budget tracking. 
-Coordinate project documentation and ensure compliance with contractual requirements. 
-Ensure company procedures and quality management systems are followed. 
-Identify opportunities to improve administrative processes and reporting efficiency. 

Essential Skills & Experience
-Diploma, Advanced Diploma or higher qualification in business, administration, information technology or a related field; or
-At least one year of equivalent industry in a similar role e.g. in contract administration, supplier coordination, commercial administration and business administration or engineering administration. 
-Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
-Strong organisational and time management abilities. 
-High level of attention to detail. 
-Ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. 
-Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel and Word. 
-Experience maintaining electronic document management systems. 
-Ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary engineering teams. 

Desirable
-Experience with commercial contract management, especially within engineering, construction, mining or industrial services. 
-Exposure to Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) or technical reporting environments. 
-Understanding of quality management systems. 
-Experience supporting project delivery within technical industries.

What We Offer
Competitive salary: $79,423 per year + superannuation
Full-time permanent employment. 
Supportive and collaborative working environment. 
Exposure to major engineering and infrastructure projects. 
Professional growth within Australia's engineering services industry.

result.description:
Location: Kununurra, Western Australia (East Kimberley)
Employment Type: Full-time, Ongoing (38 hours per week)

Salary: $69,000 per annum plus superannuation, with the final salary determined by qualifications and relevant experience.

About Us

Coral Coast Distributors (Cairns) Pty Ltd is a privately owned retail and distribution business operating across Northern Australia, with retail and distribution operations throughout the Kimberley region of Western Australia, the Northern Territory and Queensland.

We supply household goods and everyday essentials to regional and remote communities and pride ourselves on delivering excellent customer service, reliable product availability and efficient store operations. We offer stable, long-term employment within a supportive team environment.

The Role

We are seeking a reliable and customer-focused Retail Assistant to join our retail team in Kununurra.

This full-time position is responsible for providing excellent customer service while assisting with the day-to-day operation of the store, including merchandising, stock replenishment, cash handling and maintaining a safe and well-presented retail environment.

Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.

Key Responsibilities
Provide friendly and professional customer service.
Process customer sales using POS and EFTPOS systems.
Assist customers with product enquiries and purchases.
Receive, unpack and replenish stock.
Maintain shelves, displays and promotional merchandise.
Monitor stock levels and report inventory shortages.
Assist with stocktakes and inventory control activities.
Maintain a clean, organised and safe retail environment.
Process customer exchanges and refunds in accordance with company procedures.
Assist with opening and closing procedures, including cash handling and balancing tills.
Work collaboratively with supervisors and team members to achieve store objectives.
Perform general retail duties as required.
Skills and Experience
Previous experience in a retail or customer service environment.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Excellent customer service skills.
Ability to operate POS and EFTPOS systems or willingness to learn.
Basic computer literacy.
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to undertake manual handling tasks, including lifting and moving stock.
Willingness to work a rotating roster, including weekends where required.
Commitment to working respectfully with people from diverse cultural backgrounds.
Willingness to live and work in Kununurra, a regional location in the East Kimberley.
Desirable
Experience working in regional or remote retail environments.
Experience with stock control or inventory management systems.
Current First Aid Certificate (desirable but not essential).
Pre-Employment Requirements
National Police Check (acceptable outcome).
Applicants must have the right to work in Australia.
How to Apply

Please submit your resume together with a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience and suitability for the position.

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









About Monash Health Pathology Service 






Monash Health Pathology is an integral part of Monash Health. It is the largest public provider of Pathology services in the state and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these is located at the Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional laboratories located at the Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There is currently 22 collection locations based within the hospital sites and community settings. Services are provided to the Public and Private sectors, and other laboratory services. You will be joining Monash Health at an exciting time as we work in partnership with Alfred Health to be the premier shared public pathology service in Victoria. As a member of the pathology team you will be helping shape the direction of the partnership 












About the Role 






We are currently seeking a Medical Scientist to work within the multi-disciplinary core laboratory located at Wonthaggi Hospital. 












Role Requirements: 









The laboratory offers a 24 hour service.












On-site operational hours are 0700-2300 with on-call from 2300-0800.












The role will include out of hours shifts, weekends, on call and public holiday shifts. 












The successful applicant will be required to participate in allshifts and on call rosters. 












This position is for a temporary Parental Leave contract for 12 months. 















What you need to know:









The successful applicant will have a Degree in Applied Science (MLS) or recognised equivalent with experience in a multi-disciplinary laboratory being desirable. 












Applicants with Morphology skills will be well regarded.







For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Rebecca Davidson, Site Manager on (03) 5671 3293.


Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date. 


Applications close July 22nd, 2026.    Click here to Apply now →

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Staff Specialist in Addiction Medicine
Drug and Alcohol Clinical Services | Hunter New England Local Health District
Permanent | Up to 1.6 FTE 

Hunter New England Local Health District is seeking applications from suitably qualified Addiction Medicine specialists to join our established Drug and Alcohol Clinical Services (DACS) team. 

This is an exciting opportunity to provide contemporary, evidence-based, addiction medicine services across a diverse range of inpatient, outpatient, hospital consultation-liaison, telehealth and community-based settings throughout HNELHD, Mid North Coast and Northern NSW LHDs. The position offers flexibility, with opportunities available on a full time or part-time basis, up to a combined 1.6 FTE.

DACS aims to improve health and reduce harm for individuals, their families, carers, and the wider community. DACS provides a specialist treatment service for people with substance use issues, grounded in a Harm Minimisation model of care. DACS is a multidisciplinary service comprising nursing, medical, and allied health clinicians, alongside peer support and Aboriginal health workers. The service operates across various community, outpatient, and inpatient settings, providing prevention, early intervention, drug and alcohol assessment, treatment, counselling, and case management throughout Hunter New England Health.

About You
Applicants must be: 

Eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia as a Specialist in Addiction Medicine (or equivalent specialist qualification)

Fellow of the Chapter of Addiction Medicine, Royal Australasian College of Physicians or equivalent (eg Fellow of RANZCP with certificate of Advanced Training in Addiction Psychiatry) or overseas trained specialist pathways.

About us:
Hunter New England Local Health District is a large metropolitan and rural local health district in NSW which services a population of more than 970,000 across the Hunter, New England and Lower Mid North Coast areas. Drug & Alcohol Clinical Services are accredited to provide Addiction Medicine training by the RACP. We work in close partnership with the Calvary Mater Alcohol and Drug Service. HNELHD has strong, innovative connections with the University of Newcastle and Hunter Medical Research Institute.

Why join us?

Sustainability focus: HNELHD is committed to environmentally sustainable healthcare through energy-efficient and waste-reduction initiatives.

Staff wellbeing supports: Access to Fitness Passport, Salary Packaging, Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and a range of wellbeing initiatives.

Medical Settlement Concierge: Personalised assistance with onboarding, relocation and settling into the district - for clinicians, families and even pets.

Research and academic partnerships: Work in collaboration with the University of Newcastle and the Hunter Medical Research Institute, with opportunities to participate in research and innovation.

Why Newcastle?
Newcastle offers an unbeatable lifestyle with stunning beaches, a vibrant city culture, and easy access to the Hunter Valley wine region. Enjoy coastal living, excellent schools, and a thriving food and arts scene, all just two hours from Sydney. Whether you love surfing, hiking, or relaxing in wine country, Newcastle provides the perfect balance of career and lifestyle.
 

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Need more information? 
Click here for the Position Description 

Applications close: 10 August 2026

For more information about the role contact: Prof Adrian Dunlop - Area Director HNELHD Drug and Alcohol Clinical Services 
Ph: (02) 4016 4664 E: Adrian.Dunlop@health.nsw.gov.au 
For application related enquiries contact: Sally Jordan - Senior Medical Recruitment Consultant
Ph: (02) 4985 3353 E: Sally.Jordan@health.nsw.gov.au 

Hunter New England Local Health District (HNELHD) is dedicated to fostering a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, aligned with NSW Health's commitment to implementing the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination against Specific Diseases - this is a Category A position. Please read and understand NSW Health policy directive (PD2024_015). All new employees must agree to comply with the requirements outlined in the policy.

Workshop Service Technician – Forklifts & Material Handling

Location: Outer Eastern Suburbs, Melbourne
Work Type: Full-Time
Salary: Competitive Hourly Rate + Super + Overtime

About the Role

Are you an experienced Mechanic tired of the long city commute? We are seeking a skilled Forklift / Material Handling Technician to join our team in Melbourne’s Outer East.

In this role, no two days are the same. You will be diagnosing, servicing, and repairing a wide variety of forklifts (gas, electric, diesel) and specialized lifting equipment—both in our workshop and out in the field servicing local clients.

What We Offer

Local Work: Keep your commute short and work close to home in the outer east.
Great Variety: Work across a broad range of makes, models, and equipment types.
Competitive Pay: Excellent hourly rate with regular overtime opportunities.
Supportive Team: A modern workshop, good gear, and a friendly, down-to-earth work environment.
Key Responsibilities

Perform routine servicing, safety inspections, and breakdown repairs on various forklifts and lifting equipment.
Diagnose mechanical, hydraulic, LPG, and electrical faults efficiently.
Maintain clear service reports and communicate professionally with other staff and supervisors
Ensure all work meets strict safety standards and industry guidelines.
What We’re Looking For

Trade Qualified: Heavy Vehicle, Agricultural, Plant, or Automotive Mechanic (Cert III minimum).
Solid Experience: Proven background working on forklifts, elevated work platforms (EWPs), or heavy machinery. Car mechanics will also be considered - if you are ready for something new,
Key Skills:
Strong hydraulics and auto-electrical diagnostic skills.
LPG or Heavy Diesel experience is a major advantage.
Valid Driver’s License: Unrestricted manual driver's license required.
Self-Motivated: Able to work independently in the field and collaborate well in the workshop.
Ready to Apply?

If you're a reliable mechanic looking to secure a local role with great variety and competitive pay, we want to hear from you.

Ensuring delivery documentation is accurately completed

Demonstrable experience operating heavy rigid vehicles, preferably in a logistics or transport environment

Position: Motor Mechanic
Type: Full-time
Employer: Unique Collision Pty Ltd
Location: Huntingdale VIC 3166
Salary: $100,000 p/a
About the Business:
Unique Collision Pty Ltd is a reputable panel beating and collision repair business based in Huntingdale, Victoria, serving the greater Melbourne area. We specialise in comprehensive vehicle repair and restoration services, including insurance claims management, private work, full detailing, paintless dent removal, replacement vehicles, and free pick-up and delivery. Committed to delivering high-quality premium service, we pride ourselves on exceptional workmanship, customer satisfaction, and a supportive, team-oriented workplace culture where attention to detail and professionalism are valued.
About the Position:
As a Motor Mechanic at Unique Collision Pty Ltd, you will play a vital role in diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining vehicles to the highest standards following collision repairs and mechanical issues. This full-time position involves a broad scope of mechanical work to ensure vehicles are safe, reliable, and returned to customers in excellent condition, supporting the business’s commitment to premium service and operational efficiency in our busy collision repair workshop.
Key Responsibilities:
Diagnose mechanical and electrical faults in engines and vehicle components.
Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms, and other parts, inspecting and checking them for defects.
Repair and replace worn or defective parts, reassemble mechanical components, and refer to service manuals as required.
Perform vehicle paint preparation, mechanical repairs, and scheduled maintenance services such as oil changes and tune-ups.
Conduct final inspections, quality control checks, and testing of repaired vehicles to ensure proper performance and compliance with standards.
Dismantle and assemble vehicles as needed to support panel beating and collision repair processes.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Certificate III in relevant automotive or mechanical qualifications.
At least 2 years of industry experience as a Motor Mechanic.
Strong technical skills in diagnosing faults, mechanical repairs, electrical systems, and vehicle assembly/disassembly.
Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to high-quality workmanship.
Good interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively as part of a team in a fast-paced workshop environment.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Where there's life, there's Mercy. 

Where there's care, there's You.

Through the battles and the breakthroughs, we're there. Where will you be?

For over a century, our incredible teams have provided care for people when they need it most. Our people feel great pride in this, and they value the security and stability we offer. But it also means so much opportunity - to build on all that's gone before, to grow your impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

As a for-purpose organisation with over 10,000 dedicated, compassionate people, we continue to offer more services and deeper care than ever before. With Mercy, you'll have the chance to make an impact and gain experience that's hard to find elsewhere.

At Mercy Health, it's all about taking what we have and making it better. 

To do that, we need you. 

Join us at Mercy Health, and help our teams deliver even greater outcomes. 

About the opportunity

Mercy Place Boronia is a small traditional model nursing home located at the bottom of the Dandenong Ranges surrounded by gardens. Known for its family like atmosphere where team work is central to ensuring our residents are cared for we are an inclusive employer and keen to add the right candidate to our team.

As a Food Services Assistant you will be assisting the Chef-Cook to ensure our residents are provided with tasty, nutritious and well presented food. You will assist to maintain compliance with the food safety standards and prior experience in an aged care kitchen would be advantageous.

Assistance with delivery of food services to residents including assist with preparation of meals as required.

Ensure sufficient food & drink supplies are available in conjunction with the Chef-Cook.

Ensure individual preferences of residents and - or their dietary requirements are adhered to.

Work to local government food safety standards and follow the Food Safety Plan.

What you'll bring
 

You're resilient, compassionate and have a whole lot of heart. Most importantly, you are committed to delivering exceptional patient-centred care.

To thrive in this role, you will have:

Excellent time management, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to adapt and problem solve.

A compassionate, flexible and positive approach to effective person centred care with a focus on customer service.

The ability to nurture friendly, respectful relationships and contribute to a collaborative team environment.

Previous experience in an aged care kitchen or similar preferred.

You will also be required to provide evidence of, or in the process of obtaining:

A National Disability Insurance Scheme Workers Check OR evidence of application.

Proof of current influenza vaccination and other vaccination status consistent with public health orders.

Ready to help us shape the future of healthcare?

Join us and make a meaningful difference in people's lives - and your career.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Deliver recovery-focused mental health care across two leading services

Grow your career with education, mentoring and development opportunities

Join supportive multidisciplinary teams making a real community impact

Support recovery, deliver compassionate mental health care and build meaningful connections with consumers as part of a collaborative multidisciplinary team.

Employment Type: Permanent Full and Part Time roles available 
Position Classification: Enrolled Nurse 
Remuneration: $75,011.91 - $81,508.14 per annum - $37.83 - $41.10 per hour
Hours Per Week: up to 38
Located in: Cumberland and Blacktown Hospital 

Where you'll be working
Western Sydney Local Health District Mental Health Services offers rewarding opportunities across Cumberland Hospital and Blacktown Hospital, providing high-quality, recovery-oriented care to one of Australia's most culturally diverse communities.

Cumberland Hospital is NSW's largest and Australia's oldest mental health facility, recognised for its leadership in innovative mental health care and its commitment to respectful, person-centred practice. Blacktown Hospital provides contemporary facilities within a rapidly growing community, offering an exceptional environment for both staff and consumers.

Joining our team means becoming part of a service that values collaboration, innovation, professional growth and delivering exceptional care every day.

Work across respected mental health services at Cumberland and Blacktown Hospitals.

Be part of a supportive multidisciplinary team committed to recovery-focused care.

Access ongoing learning, clinical development and career progression opportunities.

Enjoy modern facilities, excellent transport links and convenient parking options.

Thrive in an inclusive workplace guided by our CORE Values of Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment.

What you'll be doing 
As an Enrolled Nurse, you will provide safe, compassionate and person-centred nursing care under the supervision of a Registered Nurse, supporting consumers throughout their mental health recovery journey. You'll contribute to high-quality clinical outcomes while working collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.

Deliver direct nursing care in accordance with individual care plans and your scope of practice.

Monitor, assess and report changes in consumers' health, escalating clinical concerns when required.

Support consumers with activities of daily living, therapeutic interventions and emotional wellbeing.

Maintain accurate clinical documentation and contribute to quality improvement initiatives.

Collaborate with nurses and the wider multidisciplinary team to achieve safe, effective and recovery-focused care.

Ready to make a difference?

Join Western Sydney Local Health District and help shape the future of mental health care. If you're passionate about supporting recovery, committed to delivering high-quality care and ready to grow your career within a supportive team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and bring your skills, compassion and commitment to a service where every day makes a difference.

How to Apply
Apply online by submitting your resume and addressing the criteria listed below by providing examples that demonstrate your ability before the closing date.

Essential Requirements:

Registration: Current Endorsed Enrolled Nurse Division 2 Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)

Selection Criteria:

Relevant and recent clinical experience deemed appropriate by WSLHD

Demonstrated ability to organise and prioritise work.

Demonstrated effective communication skills both written and verbal

Effective interpersonal skills showing initiative and leadership.

Ability to work as a member of a multidisciplinary team

Commitment to continuing professional development and demonstrated ability to utilise information technology within a variety of applications and willingness to undertake training.

Requisition ID: REQ677424
Applications Close: 29th July 2026

?	Ability to work independently and as part of a team

?	Supportive team environment
?	Opportunity to grow with an expanding business
